questions.q: What does an auto-compounding vault actually automate?
options: The claim-sell-restake loop, harvesting and reinvesting rewards on a schedule instead of by hand
Creating entirely new yield that didn't exist before
Removing all risk from the underlying farm
Guaranteeing a fixed APY regardless of market conditions
questions.explain: A vault doesn't invent new yield -- it captures the compounding gap a manual, infrequent claimer would otherwise leave on the table by harvesting and reinvesting automatically.

questions.q: In the lesson's worked example, how much extra does daily auto-compounding add over monthly manual compounding on $10,000 at 20% APR, before fees?
questions.explain: The lesson's math shows roughly $12,213 (daily) vs. $12,194 (monthly) -- about a $19 difference, before any vault fees.

questions.q: What does pricePerShare represent in a yield vault?
options: The dollar price of the vault's governance token
The exchange rate between vault shares and underlying assets, which rises as the strategy compounds
A fixed constant that never changes
The gas cost of depositing into the vault
questions.explain: pricePerShare = totalAssets / totalShares. As harvested rewards grow totalAssets, pricePerShare rises, so each existing share is worth more at withdrawal.

questions.q: What is a performance fee, as distinct from a management fee?
options: A fixed annual fee on total assets regardless of performance
A one-time fee charged only at deposit
A fee that only applies if the vault loses money
A percentage taken only from actual profit the strategy generates, not from principal
questions.explain: A performance fee (commonly 10-20%) is charged only on gains; a management fee (commonly 0-2%) is charged on assets regardless of performance.

questions.q: If a vault strategy earns $1,000 profit and charges a 20% performance fee, how much does the depositor keep?
questions.explain: The protocol/strategist keeps $1,000 x 0.20 = $200; the depositor keeps the remaining $800.
